source.body:
## What this is
`SERVER_UPTIME_MONITOR` is an Intent in the Telegraph catalogue. To rank its miners fairly, the network needs two things:

- **Evaluation material**: examples the network tests answers against.
- **An evaluator adapter**: the piece that scores each answer.

This Issue asks for both.

What the catalogue says it is for: Monitors synthetic HTTP/HTTPS endpoint availability, handshake latency, and uptime status from multiple edge regions.

## The Intents
Work only on these exact names.

| Intent | What it asks |
|---|---|
| `SERVER_UPTIME_MONITOR_GENERAL` | Monitors synthetic HTTP/HTTPS endpoint availability, handshake latency, and uptime status from multiple edge regions. |

## Who needs it
2 app ideas in the Season II brief need it.

Missions it serves: Consumer Automation, Mining & Power.

What those apps need from `SERVER_UPTIME_MONITOR`:
- Measure endpoint uptime from several regions.
- Return verified outage history for a cloud service endpoint.

Good evaluation material asks the kind of questions these apps will ask, so ranking rewards the miners that serve them well.

## Part 1: Evaluation material (anyone can help)
**Question pairs.** Questions people would really ask this Intent, each with a better answer and a worse answer.

The network only uses an Intent's material once enough different people have contributed. So this part needs several of you, and every person counts.

How:
1. Read [Contribute Evaluation Data](https://anjoman.ai/docs/scoring/contribute-evaluation-data). It has the row format, the limits and the reasons a row gets turned down.
2. Sign in to Anjoman and open [Evaluate](https://anjoman.ai/dashboard/eval). Add your material under the Intent's exact name from the table.
3. Check your rows. Each one should end up `eligible`. If one is `rejected`, it says why.

What makes it good:
- Use real questions people would ask this Intent.
- Make the worse answer believable but wrong, about as long as the better one, and different every time. Repeated stock answers get thrown out.
- Add the link a row came from when you can.

## Part 2: An evaluator adapter (for builders)
An adapter is a small model, packed into one `.wasm` file, that reads a question and an answer and scores the answer. You register it on the family `SERVER_UPTIME_MONITOR`, and it scores every Intent under it.

How:
1. Train and package it with [Train an Evaluator Adapter](https://anjoman.ai/docs/scoring/train-a-scoring-adapter). The kit and every command are there.
2. Register it and follow its status with [Build an Evaluator Adapter](https://anjoman.ai/docs/scoring/build-a-scoring-module). You can publish it from [Evaluate](https://anjoman.ai/dashboard/eval) in Anjoman.
3. The network tests it on this family's evaluation material, so it can only be judged once that material is in. It goes live only if it passes the network's checks.

## Rules
- Work only on the Intents in the table.
- Network details (contracts, node, chain): [Addresses & Parameters](https://anjoman.ai/docs/protocol/addresses-and-params). How Intents and families work: [Intents](https://anjoman.ai/docs/using/intents).
- Nobody from Telegraph will ask for your private key or for money.

## Done when
- [ ] Evaluation material: the network has accepted material for every Intent in the table and uses it for ranking. A maintainer ticks this once it is verified.
- [ ] Evaluator adapter: one is live on `SERVER_UPTIME_MONITOR` and scores its Intents. A maintainer ticks this once it is verified.

Your own part counts once your rows are `eligible`, or once your module passes the network's checks. Say which in your `/submit`.

## Reward
**Unfunded.** No money or tokens are paid for this Issue. The protocol's own evaluator rewards are separate: see [Tokenomics](https://anjoman.ai/docs/protocol/tokenomics). Hackathon prizes are set by the H2 rules.

## How to join
- Several people can work on this at the same time. Comment `/claim` to join. Everyone who joins is listed.
- Post `/progress <what you did>` at least every 72 hours, or your claim lapses. Other people's claims stay.
- When your part is done, comment `/submit` with your contributor address or your module's registration id, and a line on what you added.
- A maintainer checks each submission on its own. The Issue closes only when every box under "Done when" is ticked, so one part alone doesn't close it.
